new_sources.name: Survey Data Catalogue projection information
facts: all survey data is supplied in OSGB36 British National Grid with elevations above Ordnance Datum Newlyn
LIDAR Composite is transformed using OSTN15
time stamped data and point cloud data must use the metadata catalogue for the specific survey geoid model
surveys after 26 August 2016 use OSGM15 geoid model

new_sources.name: LIDAR DTM Time Stamped Tiles current dataset record
facts: archive contains site-specific DTM surveys since 1998 at 25cm 50cm 1m and 2m depending on project requirements
GeoTIFF rasters are supplied in 5km zip files aligned to OS Grid and elevations are metres referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn
transformation is specific to survey time and the metadata index is authoritative for dates resolution transform and geoid
dataset update frequency is quarterly and current record revision date is 19 July 2024
dataset period extends through 18 April 2024
coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700

new_sources.name: OS Terrain 50 grid data technical specification
facts: ASCII grid values represent pixel-centre heights
each 10km tile contains 200 by 200 pixels at 50m by 50m spacing
height values are supplied to nearest 0.1m
the GML companion carries location grid spacing vertical reference and spatial reference metadata
per-tile Metadata_<tile>.xml is supplied with flying-date information

new_sources.name: OS Terrain 50 per-tile metadata specification
facts: per-tile XML metadata follows GEMINI
projected CRS is British National Grid EPSG:27700
vertical reference is Ordnance Datum Newlyn EPSG:5701
earliest and latest flying dates are recorded for each tile where applicable
tile reference is the 10km National Grid tile reference

new_sources.name: OS Terrain 50 product supply mechanism
facts: OS Terrain 50 is available as an online download with no registration required
national ASCII GML and shapefile data is arranged in 10km by 10km tiles
the product contains 2858 tiles arranged into 55 folders representing 100km National Grid squares

new_sources.name: OS Terrain 50 source data and bare-earth modelling
facts: the source DTM is modelled as a TIN then interpolated into grid and contour products
bare-earth modelling removes buildings supported structures and vegetation while preserving terrain-significant features
X and Y are OSGB36 eastings and northings and most Z values are metres relative to Ordnance Survey Newlyn Datum
a small number of offshore islands can use local vertical datums so target metadata remains authoritative
